subject: Questions to create rasters with micro_ncep and ectotherm outputs

messages.author: 7b9976a7166ab661
messages.subject: Questions to create rasters with micro_ncep and ectotherm outputs
parts:
Hello everyone, I hope you could help me please to solve the following questions, thanks in advance. 
-Is there a way to create rasters for a given geographic area with the information of the outputs (metotut) of the micro_ncep function and outputs (environ and masbal) of the ectotherm function? 
(I have tried successfully to make rasters with runauto of microclima, but I need the information of micro_ncep and ectotherm outputs.)
-Can you replace shadow percentage values with a tree cover percentage raster? and therefore run micro_ncep and ectotherm for each cell in the raster.
-If so for both questions, would you please share with me some scripts or sources of information?
-And finally, I can get a raster of Tmax with the runauto function following the vignette, but I can't replicate it with this place: lat = 18.467429, long = -98.398995
I wrote the following code:
r <- microclima::get_dem(lat = 18.467429, long = -98.398995, resolution = 30)
temps <- microclima::runauto(r, "10/06/2010", "15/06/2010", hgt = 0.1,
               l = 1, x = 0,
               habitat = "Barren or sparsely vegetated",
               plot.progress = FALSE)
and get the following error:
       Error in compareRaster(x, extent = FALSE, rowcol = FALSE, orig = TRUE,  : 
         different resolution

Thank you very much for your time and interest.

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Questions to create rasters with micro_ncep and ectotherm outputs
parts:
Hi Israel,

If you want to generate rasters from the micro_ncep / ectotherm functions, you have to run individual simulations in a loop across a grid (you can parallelise them too) and then summarise the results per location and convert to a raster.

Re the issue of shade, it depends on the organism. You could have no tree cover at a site and yet there could be plenty of shade from bushes, and the shade required depends on the size of the organism.

Also, depending on the question you have, you may not need a super-fine spatial resolution grid but rather a representative set of point simulations.

All the best,
Mike
